chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman and others from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Do not recite poetry at night, and do not recite it in the month of Ramadan at night or during the day.' Isma'il said to him: 'O my father, for it is among us.' He said: 'Even if it is among us.'

key_terms.أَبَتَاهْ: O my father (term of respect for Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting poetry during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prohibits reciting poetry (*inshad*) during the night and specifically throughout Ramadan, day and night, to preserve the solemnity and spiritual focus of the month. When his companion Isma'il ibn Jahshan argued that poetry was a common cultural practice among the Shia, the Imam firmly replied, 'Even if it is among us,' demonstrating that customary prevalence does not exempt one from religious etiquette (*adab*) during sacred times. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between permissible cultural expressions and those that may distract from the contemplative nature of fasting.
